rationale: Evidence: iteration 1 (score 368.9) finished 16/20 oval runs, but only 1/20 s-bend and 0/20 slalom. Every failure was off_track, with max_error about 0.06 m (the off-track limit) and 1 to 2 line-loss events. The oval shows speed is adequate (about 1.8 s), so the problem is tracking, not pace. Failures happen when the line drifts past the five-sensor array (+/-0.04 m). Once it leaves the array, the robot loses the line, searches, and runs off. Changes: (1) Widen the array to seven sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.02 m steps, all at y = 0.05. With 12 mm sensors and 25 mm tape, a sensor always overlaps the tape across this span, so line loss should be rare. (2) Scale weights to x/0.04, giving (-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5). This keeps the steering gain per metre of offset the same as iteration 1, so kp stays at 2.0 and the proven gain is not disturbed. (3) Keep kd at 0.6 because oscillation was low (0.35) and the damping seems adequate. (4) Lower base_speed from 1.1 to 1.0 to give the robot more time to correct on bends. The cost is a slightly slower lap, which is a small part of the score. Mass, wheel geometry and line_loss (last_direction) stay the same to limit confounding. Expected result: no line losses on the s-bend and slalom, fewer off-track ends, and s-bend finish rate well above 5%. Hypotheses to test next: (a) if max_error stays near 0.06 with few line losses, steering lag is the limit, so raise kd or kp; (b) if line losses persist on the slalom, the search behaviour or array reach is the limit; (c) if the robot finishes but completion_time exceeds 3 s, raise base_speed back toward 1.3 to 1.5 once completion is reliable.
